ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value of $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a cube with side length labeled ℓ = 10 cm, and a symmetric regular quadrangular pyramid is placed exactly on top; the square base of the quadrangular pyramid coincides and aligns with the top face of the cube. The figure can, according to the method draft, take the height of the quadrangular pyramid as ℓ, so under the same density mp/mc = Vp/Vc = (ℓ^2·ℓ/3)/ℓ^3 = 1/3. Reasoning: To make the allowed initial velocity maximum, take the direction of motion along the diagonal of the top square, because the maximum relative sliding distance from the center to the boundary along this direction is dmax = ℓ/√2. Initially give the cube velocity v, and the quadrangular pyramid relatively lags behind. During sliding, interface friction makes the acceleration of the quadrangular pyramid μg. The cube is subject to ground friction μ(mc+mp)g and interface friction μmpg from the quadrangular pyramid, so the magnitude of the cube acceleration is μg(1+2mp/mc), in the direction opposite to the motion. The deceleration of the relative velocity is μg(1+2r)+μg = 2μg(1+r), where r = mp/mc = 1/3. Therefore the relative stopping distance s = v^2/[4μg(1+r)]. Requiring it not to exceed the maximum allowed sliding distance, let s = ℓ/√2, giving v = sqrt(4μg(1+1/3)ℓ/√2). Substituting μ = 0.3, g ≈ 10 m/s^2, ℓ = 0.10 m, v = sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2) ≈ 1.06 m/s, and according to the problem standard take approximately 1.07 m/s.

raw_record.question_text: A square-based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10\,\mathrm{cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground, and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value, $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.

method.method_draft: Use a direct force-and-kinematics sliding calculation. From the image, take the pyramid as a symmetric square pyramid centered on the cube top, with square base side equal to the cube side \(\ell=10\text{ cm}\), and with the relevant height/volume implied by the drawing so that \(m_p/m_c=V_p/V_c=1/3\). To maximize the allowed initial speed over directions parallel to the floor, choose motion along a diagonal of the square top, because the pyramid center can then move the greatest distance before reaching the boundary: \(d_{\max}=\ell/\sqrt2\). From the text, use \(\mu=0.3\), equal density, and initial cube speed \(v\) while the pyramid initially lags. During relative sliding, friction accelerates the pyramid at \(\mu g\). The cube is slowed by ground friction \(\mu(m_c+m_p)g\) and by the interface friction \(\mu m_p g\), so its acceleration is \(-\mu g(1+2m_p/m_c)\). Thus the relative speed decreases with acceleration \(2\mu g(1+m_p/m_c)\). The relative stopping distance is therefore \(s=v^2/[4\mu g(1+m_p/m_c)]\). Set \(s=d_{\max}\) and solve \(v=\sqrt{4\mu g(1+1/3)\ell/\sqrt2}\), using \(g\approx10\text{ m/s}^2\), giving about \(1.07\text{ m/s}\).

method.method_draft: Use an energy/relative-coordinate formulation instead of explicitly timing the motion. From the image, identify the same square-on-square support geometry and take the largest allowable relative displacement of the pyramid center to be the center-to-corner distance of the cube top, \(d_{\max}=\ell/\sqrt2\), achieved by choosing the initial cube velocity along a diagonal. Also use the depicted/implicit pyramid geometry to get \(m_p/m_c=1/3\). From the text, use \(\ell=0.10\text{ m}\), \(\mu=0.3\), equal density, and the fact that the pyramid is initially at rest while the cube is impulsively given speed \(v\). Treat the relative coordinate \(q=x_c-x_p\): its initial kinetic energy is \(\tfrac12 m_{\rm red}v^2\), where \(m_{\rm red}=m_cm_p/(m_c+m_p)\). The effective dissipative force opposing relative sliding is equivalently the generalized friction force that produces the relative deceleration, giving the same stopping relation \(s=v^2/[4\mu g(1+m_p/m_c)]\). Require this relative stopping distance not to exceed the diagonal support limit \(\ell/\sqrt2\). Substituting \(m_p/m_c=1/3\), \(\ell=0.10\text{ m}\), \(\mu=0.3\), and \(g\approx10\text{ m/s}^2\) yields \(v\approx1.07\text{ m/s}\).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示一个正方体放在水平地面上，边长标为 \(\ell=10\,\mathrm{cm}\)。正方体上方放着一个对称的正四棱锥，四棱锥的方形底面与正方体顶面完全重合，属于方形面对方形面的支撑几何。由图示的隐含几何，四棱锥底边为 \(\ell\)，高度取为 \(\ell\)，所以其体积为 \(\ell^3/3\)，而正方体体积为 \(\ell^3\)。两者密度相同，因此质量比为 \(m_p/m_c=1/3\)。

推理：要让金字塔底面始终与正方体顶面平行，按给定方法把限制转化为金字塔相对正方体的水平滑移距离不能超过支撑区域允许值。为了使允许滑移最大，应让初速度沿顶面正方形的对角线方向，此时从中心到角点的最大相对位移为
\[
d_{\max}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}=\frac{0.10}{\sqrt2}\,\mathrm{m}.
\]
设相对坐标 \(q=x_c-x_p\)。初始时正方体速度为 \(v\)，金字塔静止，所以初始相对速度为 \(v\)。在滑动过程中，摩擦导致相对运动减速。按指定的相对坐标/能量等效关系，相对停止距离为
\[
s=\frac{v^2}{4\mu g(1+m_p/m_c)}.
\]
要求相对停止距离不超过允许值：
\[
\frac{v^2}{4\mu g(1+m_p/m_c)}\le \frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}.
\]
代入 \(\mu=0.3\)、\(g\approx10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\)、\(m_p/m_c=1/3\)、\(\ell=0.10\,\mathrm{m}\)：
\[
v_{\max}=\sqrt{4(0.3)(10)\left(1+\frac13\right)\frac{0.10}{\sqrt2}}
\approx 1.06\,\mathrm{m/s}.
\]
按题目标准取值约为 \(1.07\,\mathrm{m/s}\)。

代入 \(\mu=0.3\)、\(g\approx10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\)、\(m_p/m_c=1/3\)、\(\ell=0.10\,\mathrm{m}\)：
\[
v_{\max}=\sqrt{4(0.3)(10)\left(1+\frac13\right)\frac{0.10}{\sqrt2}}
\approx 1.06\,\mathrm{m/s}.
\]
按题目标准取值约为 \(1.07\,\mathrm{m/s}\)。

raw_record.original_question: A square-based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10\,\mathrm{cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground, and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value, $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a cube with side length labeled ℓ = 10 cm, and a symmetric regular quadrangular pyramid is placed exactly on top; the square base of the quadrangular pyramid coincides and aligns with the top face of the cube. The figure can, according to the method draft, take the height of the quadrangular pyramid as ℓ, so under the same density mp/mc = Vp/Vc = (ℓ^2·ℓ/3)/ℓ^3 = 1/3. Reasoning: To make the allowed initial velocity maximum, take the direction of motion along the diagonal of the top square, because the maximum relative sliding distance from the center to the boundary along this direction is dmax = ℓ/√2. Initially give the cube velocity v, and the quadrangular pyramid relatively lags behind. During sliding, interface friction makes the acceleration of the quadrangular pyramid μg. The cube is subject to ground friction μ(mc+mp)g and interface friction μmpg from the quadrangular pyramid, so the magnitude of the cube acceleration is μg(1+2mp/mc), in the direction opposite to the motion. The deceleration of the relative velocity is μg(1+2r)+μg = 2μg(1+r), where r = mp/mc = 1/3. Therefore the relative stopping distance s = v^2/[4μg(1+r)]. Requiring it not to exceed the maximum allowed sliding distance, let s = ℓ/√2, giving v = sqrt(4μg(1+1/3)ℓ/√2). Substituting μ = 0.3, g ≈ 10 m/s^2, ℓ = 0.10 m, v = sqrt(4·0.3·10·(4/3)·0.10/√2) ≈ 1.06 m/s, and according to the problem standard take approximately 1.07 m/s.
